metadata.summary: Riccardo Calafiori returns to Italy with Arsenal this week - and he's a very different player compared to the one who departed for England two years ago.
metadata.content: Riccardo Calafiori: How Arsenal's defender has emerged as one of the Premier League's best left-backs | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Riccardo Calafiori: How Arsenal's defender has emerged as one of the Premier League's best left-backs Riccardo Calafiori has been called "the best left-back in the Premier League by far" by Jamie Carragher; the Italian has started the season with a goal in the Community Shield and two assists against Coventry and Aston Villa; Sky Sports' Sam Blitz analyses Calafiori's wild positioning Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Monday 7 September 2026 14:01, UK Image: Riccardo Calafiori has become a crucial cog in the Arsenal attack - as well as being a top defender Riccardo Calafiori returns to Italy with Arsenal this week - and he's a very different player compared to the one who departed for England two years ago. When Arsenal came in for Calafiori, he was regularly playing at centre-back at Bologna. Those who guided his career had doubts about whether he could reach the highest level as a left-back. But now, Calafiori is not just thriving as a left-back for the Premier League champions. "He's the best left-back in the league by far," says Jamie Carragher. metadata.content: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Tuesday | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Today on Sky Sports Racing: Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Tuesday A Grade Two scorer over hurdles back in 2024, Roadlesstravelled looks to regain the winning thread on his chase debut at Bangor-on-Dee; we have six races in all, live on Sky Sports Racing from 4.38pm Monday 7 September 2026 10:44, UK Image: Bangor is the venue for Sky Sports Racing's live action on Tuesday Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Sky Sports Racing on Tuesday. 5.12 Bangor-on-Dee - Roadlesstravelled makes chase debut Grade Two winner Roadlesstravelled makes his chase debut in the John Hewitt Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase . The seven-year-old began his career impeccably, winning three from three over hurdles, including a Grade Two novice hurdle. He has regressed markedly since, pulling up in the Formby Novices' Hurdle in December 2024, and has spent some time on the Flat since. He ran too keen on his last Flat start and returns to obstacles to make his chase debut off nearly a four-month break. He won an Irish point-to-point quite takingly back in May 2023, so if Jonjo and AJ O'Neill have got him back in decent shape, he could run a solid race. metadata.summary: Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Elena Rybakina too strong for Naomi Osaka as Qinwen Zheng comeback stuns Iga Swiatek | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Elena Rybakina too strong for Naomi Osaka as Qinwen Zheng comeback stuns Iga Swiatek Elena Rybakina beats Naomi Osaka in 66 minutes to set up a quarter-final against Qinwen Zheng, who mounted a stunning comeback to beat Iga Swiatek; Mirra Andreeva also into last eight with win over Anastasia Potapova; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 8 September 2026 07:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Naomi Osaka's match against Elena Rybakina at the US Open. Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track. Rybakina will reclaim the top spot if she reaches the semi-finals, and after dismantling two-time champion Osaka on Louis Armstrong, she has every reason to believe she can go all the way and lift the US Open trophy. It took the second seed just over 20 minutes to wrap up the first set 6-1 before securing a decisive break midway through the second to quell a resurgent Osaka and seal an emphatic 6-1 6-4 victory. metadata.content: Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash A long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the proposed clash in November; Fury called out Oleksandr Usyk on Monday Monday 7 September 2026 21:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury calls out Oleksandr Usyk in a social media video after claiming Anthony Joshua will never fight the Gypsy King Oleksandr Usyk's manager has dismissed Tyson Fury's call for a third fight with the Ukrainian amid continued doubt over an all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua. With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent. Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024. metadata.content: Isack Hadjar to miss Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid due to wrist injury as Liam Lawson continues at Red Bull | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Isack Hadjar to miss Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid due to wrist injury as Liam Lawson continues at Red Bull Red Bull confirm Isack Hadjar will miss a third straight race due to his ongoing wrist injury; Liam Lawson replaces him as Max Verstappen's team-mate again; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 8 September 2026 01:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater reveals further details about Isack Hadjar's injury ahead of the Dutch GP. Isack Hadjar will miss this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid as he continues to recover from a fractured wrist. Liam Lawson will replace Hadjar for a third successive race as Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, while Yuki Tsunoda continues at Racing Bulls. Hadjar suffered a hairline fracture in a bone in his wrist during the summer break in a routine workout that involved boxing which forced him to miss the Dutch, Italian and now Spanish Grands Prix. metadata.summary: There has been little to separate Team Europe and Team USA in recent editions of the Solheim Cup, with nothing to suggest that this week’s contest will be any different.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup 2026: How Team Europe can regain trophy and why tight contest with Team USA is expected at Bernardus Golf | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup 2026: How Team Europe can regain trophy and why tight contest with Team USA is expected at Bernardus Golf Team Europe look to regain the Solheim Cup after their 2024 loss to Team USA; Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands hosts this year's edition, where Charley Hull and Nelly Korda are the stars in action; watch live from Friday at 6am on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Tuesday 8 September 2026 06:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look back at some classic winning moments from the Solheim Cup archives There has been little to separate Team Europe and Team USA in recent editions of the Solheim Cup, with nothing to suggest that this week’s contest will be any different. Anna Nordqvist's European team look to regain the trophy on home soil at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, live on Sky Sports , two years on from a 15.5-12.5 loss in Virginia and their first defeat in the biennial contest since 2017. Whereas the Ryder Cup has typically delivered big winning margins in recent editions, aside from last year's edition at Bethpage Black and a brilliant final-day comeback from Team USA, the Solheim Cup has offered the opposite. messages.text: Leicester have sunk to new low under Martin but can he turn it around?

metadata.summary: A decade ago in September 2016, Leicester City were getting ready to play in the Champions League.
metadata.content: Leicester City sink to new low in League One but can Russell Martin turn it around? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Leicester City sink to new low in League One but can Russell Martin turn it around? Leicester City find themselves sat 17th in League One after an embarrassing 4-0 home defeat against Oxford United on Saturday; Russell Martin is already under pressure after just one win in their first five games. Monday 7 September 2026 15:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Can Russell Martin turn Leicester's fortunes around after a poor start to the season in League One - here's what the EFL Show panel think. A decade ago in September 2016, Leicester City were getting ready to play in the Champions League. Now? They sit 17th in League One, the lowest position in the club's history since they entered the Football League in 1894. Russell Martin has led the Foxes to just one win in their first five games, and on Saturday they were battered 4-0 at home by Oxford United. Leicester fans were chanting 'you're getting sacked in the morning' at Martin at the King Power Stadium, who would have been desperate for a good start to turn his reputation around after a dismal end to his time at Southampton, and then a gruelling spell at Rangers.
